title: Permanent patio program and supportive housing funding
subtitle: Also: noise cameras, fireworks review, e-scooter by-law, strategic plan and a recognition of two Special Olympics athletes.
overview: Council approved a permanent seasonal patio program for the whole city. It will run on a revenue-neutral basis, with a $10 per square metre monthly fee for patio space on the street. Any shortfall comes from the general tax levy instead of the municipal accommodation tax. Staff will report back on the program every year.

Council also passed the e-scooter by-law, which permits personal e-scooters from July 25, 2023. It approved the Future Guelph Strategic Plan for 2024-2027, with costs going to the multi-year budget process. On by-law reviews, council asked staff to report back by October on the work plan and on a fireworks review. It chose to wait for the province to allow noise cameras and to advocate for them, and it declined a review of an outdoor recreational fire by-law.

Council did not decide on a request to put up to $500,000 from the Affordable Housing Reserve into a matching fund with the Home for Good campaign. It referred the matter to staff for urgent work, which may lead to an emergency council meeting in the coming weeks. The meeting opened with a recognition of two Special Olympics World Games athletes.

decisions.detail: Council approved the strategic plan, referred implementation costs to the 2024-2027 multi-year budget process, and asked staff for an information report on key performance indicators in fall 2023.
Council approved the permanent patio program as amended to be revenue neutral, with a $10 per square metre monthly on-street fee and any shortfall covered by the general tax levy {{vote:m8}}.
Staff must report to council each year on the permanent patio program {{vote:m9}}.
Staff will report back when noise enforcement cameras become available in Ontario, and the Mayor and staff will advocate for the technology to be legislated {{vote:m16}}.
Council defeated a request for staff to report on timelines and resources for reviewing a possible outdoor recreational fire by-law {{vote:m17}}.
Staff will report back by October 2023 on timelines and resources to review the by-law on the display, sale and setting off of fireworks {{vote:m18}}.
Council approved the by-law and Traffic By-law amendments permitting personal use e-scooters effective July 25, 2023 {{vote:m20}}.

decisions.item: Home for Good matching funds request
decisions.detail: Council referred the proposed matching funds program of up to $500,000 to staff for urgent consideration, potentially leading to an emergency council meeting {{vote:m22}}.

debate: Patio fee: A downtown restaurant delegate said the $10 fee was too high given thin restaurant profit margins and compared it with Toronto's rate. One councillor said the program should be as close to revenue neutral as possible because it gives private businesses public parking space. Staff said the amendment meant a part-time administrator and a reduced level of service, but no change in cost to businesses.

Patio monitoring: Councillors wanted a follow-up report on the program. One councillor and staff cautioned that the first year would be a poor baseline, and downtown renewal work would make comparisons hard. Council chose annual reporting anyway.

Noise cameras: A resident delegate described noise as a public health issue and asked for noise camera research and advocacy. Supporters of waiting for legislation said staff time should not go to technology that is not yet legal, and that advocacy shows council is responding. The one councillor who voted against wanted staff to explore options now, and worried advocacy might rank low among provincial priorities.

Fire by-law: Opponents of a review cited smoke and air quality, and said the incoming fire chief would not support changing the by-law. A councillor in favour argued that clear rules could reduce harm, since backyard fires happen anyway.

Home for Good: Supporters stressed winter urgency, the earlier matching campaign, and the funds sitting unused in the reserve. Several councillors objected to the short notice, the lack of staff analysis and the preference for the usual request-for-proposals process. Staff said they had not been involved and needed time to understand the funding deadlines and the effect on other funders.
